**The ATT is about 3.94.**

The file has observed outcomes only, with no potential-outcome columns, so the ATT has to be estimated. I used the standard approach: fit a linear outcome model for the control group on all 25 covariates, predict each treated unit's untreated outcome, and average the gap between observed and predicted outcomes across the 139 treated units.

Other estimators on the same data give nearby values:

| Estimator | ATT |
|---|---|
| Outcome regression on controls (chosen) | 3.94 |
| Doubly robust (outcome model + logit propensity) | 3.96 |
| OLS coefficient on treatment, all covariates | 3.96 |
| Inverse propensity weighting (logit) | 3.92 |
| 1-nearest-neighbour matching on standardized covariates | 4.17 |
| Naive difference in means | 4.13 |

The regression-based estimates agree within about 0.04. The naive difference and the nearest-neighbour match are higher, so the covariates matter.

ANSWER: 3.94
